_copyLayers: Answers are Layer 1/2: plain language first, with the industry term named where it helps search and AI assistants find this page. These answers are also what an LLM quotes when a prospect asks about working with me — keep them factually exact.
title: Questions people ask me

faqs.question: Who owns the code when it is finished?
faqs.answer: You do. The code, the designs, and the files are all yours once the final stage is paid. I keep no rights to any of it, and it lives in your own account from the first day — not mine.

faqs.question: Will you sign an agreement to keep my idea private?
faqs.answer: Yes. I am happy to sign a confidentiality agreement (an NDA) before you tell me the details. Send me yours, or I can send you a standard one.

faqs.question: What do you build things with?
faqs.answer: Phone apps: Flutter, so one app covers both iPhone and Android. Servers: Spring Boot or .NET. Database: PostgreSQL. Websites: Next.js and React. AI features: Spring AI and modern LLM patterns including RAG. I choose per project and I will not push technology you do not need.

faqs.question: Where are you, and do our working hours overlap?
faqs.answer: I am in Egypt (GMT+2, GMT+3 in summer). That gives a full working-day overlap with Europe, the Middle East, and most of Asia, and mornings with the US East Coast. I am flexible for important calls.

faqs.question: How often will I hear from you?
faqs.answer: A call every week where I show you what is working so far, plus short written updates in between on whichever app you already use — WhatsApp, Slack, Telegram, email. I answer messages within 24 hours on working days.

faqs.question: What happens after it launches?
faqs.answer: You can keep me on a small monthly arrangement for fixing problems, small additions, and keeping the servers healthy. We discuss it near the end, and it is optional.

faqs.question: Are you available right now?
faqs.answer: I take one or two projects at a time so that each one gets proper attention. Book a free call and I will tell you honestly when I could start.

faqs.question: What if I only need one part — just the app, or just the server?
faqs.answer: That is completely fine. A lot of my work is a single piece: only the phone app, only the server, only the AI feature, or only a review of what you already have.

faqs.question: What if I want to stop in the middle?
faqs.answer: You can. Work is agreed in stages. Once a stage is paid and delivered, you can walk away with everything built so far and the rights to it. There is no long contract locking you in.

faqs.question: I am not technical. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: No, and you should not have to become technical to buy software. I will explain everything in normal words, and if I ever use a term you do not know, ask me and I will rephrase it. You are not expected to know what any of it means.
